styles.name: Inshore & flats
styles.definition: Fish sheltered bays, estuaries, mangroves or shallow saltwater flats. The water and tide shape the day.
styles.suits: Anglers who want short casts, shallow water and a smaller-boat trip.
styles.gear: Skiffs and bay boats are common choices. Match spinning or fly tackle to the target, cover and wind.
styles.season: Ask about tide, water clarity and wind as well as the month.

styles.name: Offshore & bluewater
styles.definition: Travel beyond the sheltered coast to fish open water. Trolling, casting and other methods depend on the target.
styles.suits: Anglers comfortable with longer boat runs and changing sea conditions.
styles.gear: A charter boat, suitable safety equipment and guide-selected tackle form the starting point. Confirm the run time and supplied equipment.
styles.season: Ask about the target’s local window and a weather alternative. A calendar month does not predict sea conditions.

styles.name: Surf & pier
styles.definition: Fish from the beach, rocks or a pier. Access, casting space and surf conditions set the limits.
styles.suits: Anglers who prefer a shore-based day and can adapt to local access conditions.
styles.gear: Shore tackle, a suitable landing method and secure footwear matter. Confirm the cast, current and allowed access before choosing weights.
styles.season: Ask how tides, swell and local fish movements affect the proposed date.

styles.name: Fly fishing
styles.definition: Present a fly with a fly rod. This method spans small streams, large rivers and saltwater flats.
styles.suits: Anglers who enjoy presentation and want to practise casting or learn with a guide.
styles.gear: Choose the rod, line, leader and flies for the target and water. A wade, boat or skiff trip needs a different access plan.
styles.season: Match the date to local water conditions and the target. A hatch is a local event, not a worldwide season.

styles.name: River float & drift boat
styles.definition: Cover a river reach from a moving boat. The launch, take-out and river level are part of the trip plan.
styles.suits: Anglers who want to cover more water with a guide or a planned shuttle.
styles.gear: A drift boat, raft or local river boat may suit the reach. Confirm the craft, flotation equipment and tackle with the operator.
styles.season: River level and flow can change the route. Ask about the exact reach and a high-water alternative.

styles.name: Lake & reservoir
styles.definition: Fish enclosed freshwater, from a large reservoir to a smaller lake. Depth, access and species determine the method.
styles.suits: Anglers who want to choose between bank access and a boat day.
styles.gear: Bank tackle or a guide’s boat setup can work. Confirm the launch, target depth and method before packing.
styles.season: Water temperature, lake level and local fish movements matter. Use the documented windows below as a starting point.

styles.name: Ice fishing
styles.definition: Fish through ice with a locally assessed access plan. A winter date alone does not establish safe ice.
styles.suits: Anglers who want a winter trip and can confirm suitable local support.
styles.gear: Ice tackle, warm layers and locally specified safety equipment are needed. Confirm shelter, transport and guide provisions.
styles.season: The trip depends on current local ice conditions. Do not use the month filter as an ice-safety test.

styles.name: Fly-in & remote lodge
styles.definition: Use a remote lodge or an air transfer as the base for a fishing trip. Travel and equipment limits shape the plan.
styles.suits: Anglers who want several days based near remote water and can accept travel changes.
styles.gear: Confirm aircraft baggage limits, transfers, boats, guide support and supplied tackle directly with the lodge.
styles.season: Operating dates and weather delays differ by lodge. Confirm the transfer schedule and a spare travel day.

styles.name: Kayak fishing
styles.definition: Fish from a small paddle or pedal craft. The route, launch and weather plan are as important as the tackle.
styles.suits: Anglers who want close access and can meet the physical and safety needs of the chosen water.
styles.gear: Confirm the kayak, personal flotation equipment, secure tackle storage and return route. Ask whether instruction or a guide is available.
styles.season: Wind, tides, current and water temperature can change the route. Confirm conditions close to departure.

styles.name: Bottom fishing & combo charters
styles.definition: Fish near the bottom for local targets, or combine supported fisheries in one boat day. A combo depends on time and conditions.
styles.suits: Anglers who want a boat trip focused on reef, rock or bottom habitat.
styles.gear: Boat tackle and weights must suit the depth, current and target. Ask what the crew supplies and how the day divides between targets.
styles.season: Species windows and local rules may differ within one trip. Confirm each target and the available boat time.

styles.name: Night fishing
styles.definition: Fish after dark with a plan for visibility, access and the return. The method depends on the place and target.
styles.suits: Anglers comfortable with reduced visibility and a later or overnight schedule.
styles.gear: Confirm lighting, safe access, communication and suitable tackle. On a charter, ask about rest space and the total trip length.
styles.season: Ask which local conditions support the night method. Do not assume that a daytime season also supports a night trip.

styles.name: Sight fishing
styles.definition: Locate a visible fish before the cast. Light, clarity and a careful approach are central to the method.
styles.suits: Anglers who enjoy observation, accurate casts and patient presentations.
styles.gear: Polarized glasses and a target-specific setup can help. A skiff or a wade trip needs a separate access plan.
styles.season: Ask about light, wind, tides and clarity. A local monthly window cannot guarantee visibility.

styles.name: Big-game & billfish
styles.definition: Plan a boat trip around large pelagic fish such as billfish or tuna. The target and local method define the tackle.
styles.suits: Anglers who want a focused offshore trip and can meet its physical and time demands.
styles.gear: Confirm the boat, tackle class, fish-handling plan and crew support. Do not buy specialist tackle before checking the charter’s provisions.
styles.season: Ask about the named target’s local window and current rules. The records below retain their own season evidence.

styles.name: Multi-species slams
styles.definition: Work toward a locally defined group of species in one trip. The meaning of a slam changes with the region.
styles.suits: Anglers who value variety and can adjust the plan as tides and conditions change.
styles.gear: Several presentations may be needed. Confirm each target, suitable tackle and whether the operator treats the slam as a goal.
styles.season: Look for an overlap between the target species. A slam is an objective, never a promised result.

styles.name: Bank & wade
styles.definition: Reach the water from shore or by wading. Access rights, footing, depth and current set the practical limits.
styles.suits: Anglers who prefer to stay close to shore or explore a short stretch on foot.
styles.gear: Choose footwear, clothing and tackle for the water. Ask whether waders or a wading staff are appropriate for the exact reach.
styles.season: Water level and temperature affect access. Confirm the route and conditions, even within a documented seasonal window.

styles.name: River & stream
styles.definition: Fish flowing freshwater from the bank, by wading or from a boat. The reach and water level shape the day.
styles.suits: Anglers who want to explore current, pools and changing river habitat.
styles.gear: Match tackle to the target and flow. Choose the access method separately, then confirm the launch or bank route.
styles.season: Ask about flow, temperature and local restrictions for the exact reach. Some catalog records have no verified month window.
